First day in the new uniform

👕📷
Nilufar · Jasur · 8:10 a.m.
NilufarGood morning, Jasur! Are you wearing the new uniform today?
JasurYes, I am! I am wearing a blue shirt and grey trousers. My mum is taking a photo of me now. She is very happy!
NilufarMe too! I am wearing a white shirt and a blue skirt. My little sister is wearing her uniform too, but it is too big for her! Mum says she can make it smaller tonight.
JasurHa ha! What is your brother doing? Is he ready for school?
NilufarHe is looking for his shoes. He is always late! Look — here is my photo. Do you like my uniform? They are under his bed, of course! Now he is running to the kitchen for breakfast.
JasurIt is great! See you at school. You look very smart in it. My bus is coming now — bye!

📧 Email

An email to my cousin

📚✏️
From: Dilnoza · To: Sevara

Hi Sevara! How are you? I am writing this email at seven o'clock. I am not doing my homework right now — I am having a short break!

I usually do my homework in the kitchen, because my room is very cold. But today the kitchen is very noisy. My grandmother is cooking and my little brother is singing. It is not quiet at all! My grandmother gives me tea and bread while I work, so the kitchen is also the best place!

My mother always helps me with maths. She is good at numbers. My father helps me with English. Tonight I have maths, English and history. I want to finish before nine o'clock. He is only four years old and he sings the same song ten times every evening.

Where do you do your homework? Is your house quiet? Write soon! Maths is easy for me but history is difficult, because there are many dates.

Dilnoza

🌐 Blog

This year I am trying everything!

♟️⚽
Aziz's blog · September

Hello! My name is Aziz and I am twelve. This year is my best school year. I am doing three new things!

First, I am in the chess club. We meet on Mondays. I am learning new moves and I practise every evening with my grandfather. He always wins, but I am getting better! Our club has twelve students and one old chess board.

Second, I am playing football. Our team is small but fast. We practise on Wednesdays after school. Our teacher, Mr Karimov, is a very good coach. Last Saturday we played against School 22 and we won two goals to one!

Third, I am learning English with my friend Shoxrux. We watch short films and we write new words in a little book. We have 200 words now! My favourite new word this month is “amazing”.

What are you doing this year? Tell me in the comments!

✉️ Letter

A note for Bobur

🥚🛒
On the kitchen table

Dear Bobur,

I am at work today. Please go to the market after school. Here is your shopping list.

There are no eggs in the fridge, so please buy ten eggs. There are some apples, but there are only two. Please buy six more. Are there any tomatoes? I think there are three, but they are very small. Buy eight, please. There is some rice in the big blue box, so we do not need any rice this week.

There is no bread. Buy two loaves. There is some cheese and there is some butter, so do not buy them. There are no onions either. Please buy one kilo.

The money is in the blue cup. Thank you, my dear son! Please come home before six o'clock, because your grandmother is coming for dinner.

Mum

🎤 Interview

Ten minutes in Aziza's shop

🍚🛍️
Our school magazine · Shop corner

Reporter: Good morning, Aziza. You work in this little shop. What do people buy every day?

Aziza: Good morning! Every day people buy rice, bread and oil. A big box of rice is very popular. My shop is small, but we have everything for a good dinner.

Reporter: How much rice is in one box?

Aziza: There are five kilos in one box. It is heavy, so I always help my customers carry it to the car. Many families buy one box every month.

Reporter: And how many bottles of water do you sell?

Aziza: About one hundred bottles every day! In summer we sell more. Children come here after school and they always want cold water and ice cream.

Reporter: Thank you, Aziza. Have a good day! Come again and bring your friends!

📔 Diary

Monday, 9 October

🍽️🌙
Shahnoza's diary

Today is a normal Monday. I get up early, at half past six. I always have bread and tea for breakfast. My brother never eats breakfast — he says he is not hungry! He only drinks a glass of milk and runs to the bus.

School starts at eight. I come home at two o'clock and I do my homework. Then I help my mother in the kitchen. On Mondays I also have a music lesson at four o'clock.

In my family we eat dinner very late, at nine o'clock. My father works until eight, so we wait for him. We all eat together and we talk about our day. I like this time very much. My little cousin always falls asleep at the table!

After dinner I am very tired. I read for ten minutes and then I sleep. Tomorrow is Tuesday — I have English!

📰 Article

Our class travels to school

🚌🚲
School newspaper · Class 6B

Last week we asked all 24 students in our class one question: how do you get to school?

Twelve students walk. They live near the school, so they only need ten minutes. “I walk with my sister every morning,” says Malika. “It is good exercise and it is free,” she says.

Six students take the bus. The bus stops in front of the school. Sardor lives far away, so his journey takes thirty minutes. He gets up at six o'clock every morning to catch it.

Four students come by bicycle. They are fast and they are never late! Two students take the metro with their father. “I am never in traffic,” says Jasur, “and my bicycle is red and very fast.”

And our teacher? She drives a small red car. “The traffic is terrible,” she says. “Next year I want a bicycle too!” We think that is a very good idea!

🌐 Blog

My mum and dad at work

🩺🚕
Kamola's blog · Tuesday

My mother is a doctor. She works in a big hospital in our city. She starts very early, at seven o'clock in the morning. She helps children and she is very kind. Sometimes she comes home late, but she is never angry. Her favourite patients are the small children, because they are very brave.

My father is a taxi driver. He works in the afternoon and in the evening. He knows every street in our city! He tells us funny stories about his customers at dinner. On Sundays he does not work, and we all go to the park together.

My grandmother does not work now, but she was a teacher for thirty years. Many people in our street say, “Good morning, teacher!” to her. She still helps me with my reading every evening.

I am very proud of my family. And I want to be a doctor, like my mother.

📖 Story

The empty battery

📱🔌
A short story

It was Friday afternoon. Otabek had a big problem: his phone battery was at two per cent and his project was on the phone. He had only twenty minutes before the lesson.

“Can I borrow your charger?” he asked Nodira. “I am sorry,” she said, “my charger is at home. But you can use my laptop.”

“Thank you!” said Otabek. “Can I use your headphones too?” Nodira smiled. “Yes, you can. But please be careful with them — they are new.” Otabek was very careful. He put them on the table, not on the floor.

Otabek finished his project on the laptop. Then he gave everything back. “Thank you, Nodira. You saved my project!” The project was about the planets and it had fifteen pictures.

“No problem,” said Nodira. “But next Friday — bring your own charger!”
